newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-ELIGIBILITY RULES NEED TIGHTENING.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-ELIGIBILITY RULES NEED TIGHTENING.

text.p: Eligibility rules have to change before next year's Winter Olympics to combat the risk of court action, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said on Friday.

The IIHF's tight eligibility regulations have been thrown into question by Alexander Mogilny of the Vancouver Canucks who has indicated he wants to play for the United States in Nagano, where professionals will be allowed to compete for the first time.
But Mogilny has represented Russia at a world championship and the rules state that players cannot play for other countries.

IIHF president Rene Fasel said the governing body had not been threatened by Mogilny, now an American citizen, or the United States Ice Hockey Federation with court action if the rules are not amended. But he did acknowledge that if the case went to court the IIHF would lose.
"We have to adjust our rules because right now if we went to court there is a 99 percent chance we would lose," said Fasel on the eve of the world championships.
"We don't want a judge coming along saying a player has the right to play for this country or that country. We don't like going to court.
"It must be our decision or we change rules so they are acceptable to a judge in court."
The IIHF will discuss possible changes during the second week of the championships, subject to approval by an extraordinary congress in September.
